# Yellow-naped Amazon Parrot

The Yellow-naped Amazon is a robust Central American parrot named for its yellow nape. Known for an expressive voice and strong personality, it needs skilled, consistent handling and an environment ready for noise and activity.

Scientific nameAmazona auropalliata

Typical adult sizeAbout 35–38 cm long; approximately 450–600 g, with individual variation.

Lifetime planningA multi-decade commitment is possible; published estimates vary and are not guarantees.

## Overview and appearance

Yellow-naped Amazons are mostly green, with a bright yellow patch at the nape that can become more noticeable as a bird matures. Blue may show on the forehead, with other yellow facial markings varying between individuals. Their sturdy body and hooked bill are typical of medium-to-large Amazons.

The species is native to Central America. A companion bird remains active, social and vocal. Its distinctive colour and reputation for mimicking songs are not a substitute for learning the needs and signals of the individual bird.

## Temperament and social needs

Yellow-naped Amazons are often described as bold and expressive, but there is no predictable temperament shared by every individual. They can be sensitive to handling, particularly when excited or uncertain. Respectful boundaries, patient observation and steady routines are important for safe interaction.

A bird needs daily engagement and opportunities to occupy itself, rather than constant attention from a single person. Maturity and breeding-related behaviour can influence some individuals, so plan for changing needs and seek professional behavioural support when challenges arise. Do not assume sex determines a bird’s personality.

## Typical adult size

This Amazon is generally around 35–38 cm long, with a broad typical weight range of roughly 450–600 g. Size varies, and weight alone is not a full measure of condition. A sturdy enclosure should allow climbing and wing stretching, with regular supervised movement in a safely prepared room.

## Expected lifespan and long-term care

The species can be long-lived, and a commitment spanning decades is possible. Estimates differ, so it is more prudent to plan for a substantial care horizon than to treat a single number as typical or guaranteed. Consider a contingency guardian and ongoing care costs.

## Talking and vocalisation

This species is notably vocal and some individuals can imitate speech, music or household sounds. Neither talking nor a manageable noise level is guaranteed. Loud calls may be part of normal communication, which makes a quiet flat or noise-sensitive household a poor assumption without careful consideration.

## Intelligence and reward-based training

Use positive reinforcement to teach cooperative everyday skills, such as waiting on a perch and entering a travel carrier. Short training sessions, foraging games and safe puzzles give the bird constructive work. Consistent routines and reading body language matter more than trying to suppress normal vocal behaviour through punishment.

## Diet and nutrition

A balanced diet should include appropriate formulated food and a variety of fresh vegetables, with fruit and rich treats considered in moderation. Avoid a seed-based menu as the default. An avian veterinarian can help assess the individual bird’s food, condition and any planned changes; do not use supplements without specific advice.

## Housing, exercise and enrichment

Provide secure housing with varied perches, safe exercise and enrichment suited to a strong beak. Daily activity should combine social contact, climbing and food-searching. Rotate and inspect toys, keep the room safe, and provide a calm resting area away from household traffic.

## Suitability and questions before enquiring

A Yellow-naped Amazon is best considered by people ready for an assertive, vocal parrot and able to offer consistent routines, meaningful activity and respectful handling. It is not an automatic beginner choice. Families need adult supervision, clear boundaries and a way to give the bird space when it prefers not to interact.

Ask about this individual’s history, vocal habits, diet, routine and handling experience. Think through the household’s noise tolerance and long-term care plan, then confirm current individual availability directly. This page is educational; it does not promise that a Yellow-naped Amazon is in stock.
